name: District of Columbia

sales.rateNote: District-wide general rate of 6%; there are no separate local taxes. The scheduled increase to 7% has been postponed: OTR states the general rate remains 6% through September 30, 2027. Higher rates apply to restaurant meals (10%), off-premises alcohol and rental cars (10.25%), hotels (15.95%) and parking (18%).

scheduledChanges.what: Postponed increase of the general rate to 7%: OTR says 6% remains through September 30, 2027. (The codified D.C. Code § 47-2002 still reads 7% from October 1, 2026.)
The temporary 15.95% hotel rate is extended through September 30, 2027 (Hotel Surtax Amendment Act of 2025).

local.levies: none: DC is a single taxing jurisdiction

groceries.note: SNAP-eligible food or drink is excluded from retail sales, except food prepared for immediate consumption and soft drinks (soft drinks are taxed at 8%).

clothing.note: Clothing is taxed at the 6% general rate.

otherRates.item: restaurant meals, prepared food and on-premises alcohol
parking or storing of motor vehicles

sales.holidayNote: No general sales tax holiday in 2026.

useTax.note: Use tax is due at the same rates as sales tax on taxable items bought for use in DC without DC sales tax.

facts.text: The increase of DC's general sales tax to 7% has been postponed; the rate stays 6% through September 30, 2027.
The Sales Tax Increase Delay Amendment Act of 2025 had already kept the rate at 6% through September 30, 2026.
DC applies seven different rates, from 6% on general goods to 18% on parking.
Medicines and drugs are exempt whether or not sold on prescription.
Street and mobile food vendors pay 10% on food and 6% on other sales, with a minimum of $375 per quarter.
Late returns incur a 5% to 25% penalty plus 10% annual interest compounded daily.

property.levied: The District government levies and collects real property tax directly (OTR); rates per class are set each year by the Council of the District of Columbia.

assessment.text: Property is assessed annually at estimated market value. Tax = assessed value / 100 x class rate: Class 1A residential $0.85 per $100; Class 1B (up to two units) $0.85 on the first $2.558 million and $1.00 above; commercial $1.65 to $1.89; vacant $5.00; blighted $10.00. Homesteaded owners cannot be taxed on more than a 10% yearly increase in assessed value (2% for seniors and disabled owners).

homestead.name: Homestead Deduction
homestead.text: Reduces the assessed value of an owner-occupied principal residence by $91,950 for tax year 2026, saving $781.58 a year at the $0.85 rate (it was $89,850 for tax year 2025).
homestead.applyBy: Apply online with form ASD-100 on MyTax.DC.gov; an application approved between October 1 and March 31 gives the full year, April 1 to September 30 gives half.

otherRelief.name: Senior Citizen or Disabled Property Owner Tax Relief
otherRelief.text: Cuts the property tax by 50% for owners aged 65+ or disabled who own at least 50% of the home, within the household income threshold ($159,750 for tax year 2025).

otherRelief.name: Assessment Cap Credit
otherRelief.text: Homesteaded property is not taxed on more than a 10% annual increase in assessed value; 2% for senior and disabled owners.

otherRelief.name: Disabled Veterans' Homestead Deduction
otherRelief.text: Separate deduction for disabled veterans owning at least 50% of the home; not combinable with the regular homestead deduction, senior relief or cap credit.

dueDates.text: Two installments: first half (October 1 - March 31) due by March 31; second half (April 1 - September 30) due by September 15.

facts.text: OTR's example: a $500,000 home in Class 1A owes $4,250 a year before the homestead deduction and credits.
Class 1B taxes the part of a one- or two-unit home's value above $2.558 million at $1.00 per $100 instead of $0.85.
The homestead deduction is $91,950 for tax year 2026, worth $781.58 a year.
Vacant property is taxed at $5.00 and blighted property at $10.00 per $100, to push owners to use or repair it.
DC reassesses all real property every year.
